nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $c$, fewer than $2^{n-c}$ binary strings of length $n$ have Kolmogorov complexity less than $n - c$, where $n - c$ is read as $0$ when $c > n$.
nodes.title: Most strings are incompressible

nodes.summary: Fewer than `2 ^ m` strings have complexity below `m`. Padding their shortest descriptions to length `m` maps them injectively to strings of length `m` other than `0ᵐ`.
nodes.title: Few strings have small complexity

nodes.summary: Some string of length `n` has complexity at least `n`.
nodes.title: Incompressible strings exist at every length

nodes.summary: The function sending each binary string $x$ to its Kolmogorov complexity $K(x)$ is not computable: no partial recursive function, acting on binary strings through their encodings as natural numbers, halts on every binary string $x$ with output $K(x)$.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov complexity is not computable

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a binary string $p$, the padding of $p$ to length $n$ is the string $0^k 1 p$ with $k = \max(n - 1 - |p|, 0)$; when $|p| < n$ it has length $n$.
nodes.title: Padding a string to a given length

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the finite set of all binary strings of length $n$.
nodes.title: Binary strings of a given length
